(p-١) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Saff, also called al-Hawariyyun (the Disciples).

Its purpose is to urge complete striving in unity of heart in the jihad against those whom al-Mumtahanah called to disavowal of them, by compelling them to the true religion, or by bringing them to the furthest edge of the earth's extremity, in order to exalt the Most High King above associating partners and to protect His most holy Presence from falsehood, and as proof of sincerity in disavowing them and being hostile to them. Thus it is the outcome of Surah al-Tawbah, and what is in it that points most clearly to this purpose is al-Saff, through reflection on its verse and contemplation of the great benefit it contains at its beginning, its middle, and [its end]. Likewise the Hawariyyun. "In the name of Allah" (the greatest King, to whom all command belongs, for there is no equal to Him). "The Most Gracious" (who has encompassed, by the blessing of clear expression, all that pleases Him, to whoever opposes Him; for He has prescribed for everyone that he may either reject it or accept it). "The Most Merciful" (who has singled out, by the completion of favour that leads to the Abode of Peace, whomever of His servants He wills, preparing and qualifying him for that).

* *

(p-٢) When al-Mumtahanah concluded with the command to exalt Him, glorified is He, above allegiance to those who oppose His command, by turning away from them and disavowing them, following the people of the ranks who are detached from everything other than Allah, especially those who, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," became arrogant, al-Saff opened with what is, as it were, the cause of that. So He said: ﴿Glorifies Allah﴾, that is: He brought about the greatest exaltation of the greatest King, to whom belongs ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾ of all things, of which none is heedless: their spheres and stars, and other substances and accidents, in their rising and setting, their motion in going and returning, the forming of clouds, the sending down of waters, and other things. And since the address was with those other than the sincere, He emphasized it, so He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, that is, by carrying out all that is required of it, which is like what is commanded in relation to the actions of rational beings: the descent of waters, the bringing forth of plants from the herb and the tree, the ripening of grains and fruits, and other matters, small and great.

And since the obedience of the non-rational and the disobedience of the rational may give rise to an appearance of deficiency, He said: ﴿And He﴾, that is, alone, with no partner, ﴿is the Almighty﴾, that is, the One of great benefit who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything, and whom reaching is difficult; ﴿the All-Wise﴾, that is, the One who places things in their most perfect positions. Thus He allowed the rational to commit disobedience only to manifest the attributes of perfection: knowledge, power, forbearance, generosity, mercy, (p-٣) wrath, and others. He knew by this exaltation, and concluded its verse with these two attributes, that He, exalted is He, is far above what the unbelievers' despair, mentioned there, contains, [namely] that there is no resurrection, and above His giving them any share in the Hereafter, for each of the absence of resurrection and the equating of the evildoer with the doer of good is a deficiency.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: It was opened with the glorification because of what Surah al-Mumtahanah ended with, namely His saying: ﴿Do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 13], and they are the Jews. The indication of what made them deserving of this has already preceded, so it was followed by exaltation, in accordance with what has been explained, for it is something that is mentioned after the recounting of crimes committed, and does not occur otherwise. Then He followed that with commanding the servants to fulfil their pledges, which He had set forth in al-Mumtahanah, so that they might be exalted above the condition of those deserving wrath, through the opposite of fulfilment: opposition in the hearts [and tongues]: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 11]; ﴿Twisting their tongues and slandering the religion﴾ [al-Nisa': 46]; ﴿Among those who say, "We believe," with their mouths, while their hearts have not believed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41]; ﴿They say, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey," then a faction of them turns away﴾ [al-Nur: 47]. By all of this together they gathered cursing and wrath, so it was said to the believers: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [al-Saff: 2], beware that your conditions resemble the condition of those who deserved hatred, cursing and wrath. Then He followed this with the good recompense for whoever fulfils in word, in pledge, in tongue and in heart, and remains steadfast in [what] he was commanded: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks﴾ [al-Saff: 4], the verse, and then what follows is interwoven. And since what came of this purpose in Surah al-Mumtahanah came in the manner of counsel and the way of advice and compassion, He followed in Surah al-Saff with explicit reproach for it and rebuke, so that, after [what] was laid down in the preceding surah, it would be more effective in censure. Consider how great is the difference between His saying, glorified is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], with what it contains of gentleness, and His saying: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [al-Saff: 2], ﴿It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 3]. End.

And when the great conquest was mentioned in Al-Mumtahanah, in the story concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a, may Allah be pleased with him, and the rebuke of the disbelievers in every respect, it established the soundness of the emigration and claimed the readiness for jihad against the enemies of Allah. The story of the conquest that was a cause, concerning the prohibition of believing women to the polytheists and the prohibition of polytheists to believing women, took place at the Battle of al-Hudaybiyya. In this, Allah, glory be to Him, displayed among His artful works, which the powers of creation cannot match, that the ranking of what is in the conquest that was a cause is placed above what is in the true practical conquest. So He made the first, in time, last in rank, and the second, in time, first in rank, together with great precision in the arrangement of the system and an eloquence and harmony that the perceptions of minds cannot bear, along with the novelty of the meanings and the solidity of the structures. The act of one who advised the disbelievers, from among those who had believed with his tongue, had submitted with his heart, and had emigrated with his limbs, was a kind of advising through the act of one who says what he does not do [in opposing them and in dissociating from their enmity, so He mentioned at the beginning of this surah His exoneration through the tongues of the states of what does not understand] that which shames the Muslim with any of that, as a discipline for the likes of him, and as training for whoever is touched by some opposition in his mind. The intellectual person is more fitting than others to exonerate the sacred presence through obedience, so how [if] he is one who has affirmed faith and undertaken the obligation of submission? Whoever among them disobeys is calling out against himself by the contradiction of his speech to his deeds, while whoever exonerates Him with the due exoneration does not fall short in any of His rights by neglecting any of His commands, just as exonerating what does not understand is by not opposing any of His wishes. He said, frightening with the call of distance and rebuke, which is among the beginnings of anger and denial, by the interrogative and by expressing with what conveys the lowest level of faith: ﴿O you who believe﴾, that is, those who claimed faith. ﴿Why﴾. In al-Kashshaf it is said: it is the lam of attribution entering upon the interrogative "mā", just as other prepositional particles entered upon it, as in bima, fima, mimma, amma, ila-ma, and 'alama. The alif was omitted only because "mā" and the preposition are like one thing. Its use occurred with the addition of the hā' al-sakt (the silent hā') or with the sukūn (vowellessness). Whoever pauses in connection does so by treating it as a pause, as was heard in thalathah arba'ah with the hā' and the transfer of the hamza's vowel onto it, the hamza being elided. Al-Radi said concerning the relative: it was omitted because it has the front of the sentence, and it was not possible to delay the preposition past it, so he placed it first and compounded it with [until] the whole becomes a term set for interrogation, so the interrogation does not fall from the rank of the front, and he made the omission of the alif an indication of composition. ﴿You say﴾, that is, from the claim of faith whose requirement is the obligation of sincerity in all states, ﴿what you do not do﴾, that is, what you do not truly affirm by the deed that would be with the utmost desire and strength, so that you would take the enemy as an ally by turning toward him and sending advice to him, while you have uttered faith, which necessitates enmity toward everyone who disbelieves. And breaking a promise within oneself is [ugly], and with the Creator it is uglier.

When that would have been destructive, He, out of mercy toward those addressed, made it great in their estimation so that they might save [themselves] by refraining from it. So He said: ﴿Most hateful it is﴾. By this He intended amazement (*ta'ajjub*), which is the magnifying of the matter in the hearts of the listeners, because amazement occurs only at a matter that stands outside its like and kind. He explained what He intended by it, to show its purity in hatred, with His words ﴿in hatred﴾, meaning, in great magnitude. How greatly hateful it is, a hatred that is the most intense of hatreds. He increased its abhorrence, adding further to the aversion from it, with His words ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King before whom every self-aggrandizer is held in contempt. When He had made its abhorrence complete, the soul longed for the one to whom this would be attributed, so He said: ﴿that you say﴾, that is, a great matter from that direction (p-7) that may occur at some time or in some state, your saying ﴿what you do not do﴾.

Al-Qushayri said: [It is said]: Allah did not threaten anyone for a slip with the like of what He threatened for this. End of quote.

Everything they mentioned concerning its cause is suitable as a cause. Among these is the statement of some of them: "If we knew which deed is most beloved to Allah, we would strive for it," and then they turned away on the day of Uhud. Some of them were remiss in jihad. And the matter of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, who killed on the day of Badr a man who had harmed the Muslims and inflicted great harm upon them, while another claimed that he had killed him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased, so Umar and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has reported that you killed him." Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I killed him only for Allah and His Messenger." Then Umar and Abd al-Rahman, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Is it so, Abu Yahya?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." And [the cause is] the commitment of the hypocrites to the rulings of Islam and their failure to follow through, a breach in great matters. Likewise is the story of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him.

When the thing he dislikes grew great, after he had set ablaze the glorifying of what is not rational, and the rational one was deserving of asking about what he loves so that he might glorify Him with it, He said, mentioning the end that is the comprehensive "mother" (umm) of all the excellences that precede it, emphasizing because the address is with one who falls short or is in his judgment: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belong all the attributes of (p-٨) perfection, ﴿loves﴾, that is, He acts the act of one who loves, toward ﴿those who fight﴾, that is, those who bring about fighting, ﴿in His cause﴾, that is, on account of making easy His path that leads to His pleasure, a fighting enclosed within the path, such that no part of it is like a thing outside of it. So they fight the enemies of the religion, from the devils, with remembrance of the heart and the tongue, and from humans, with the sword and the spear. ﴿In ranks﴾, that is, lined up, so that, in the unity of their purpose, they are as if they were one heart, just as they were equal in lining up, like one body.

Since lining up would be true even with slight advancing and lagging, He negated that by His saying, state after state: ﴿as if they were﴾, that is, from the intensity of their closeness and equality in chests and shoulders and steadfastness in their positions, ﴿a structure﴾. He added to the emphasis by His saying ﴿well-compacted﴾, that is, of great connection and strong firmness, as if it had been fused with lead, so there is no gap in it and no defect. For whoever is like this is deserving that none of his deeds contradict any of his words. So "compacting" is an indication of the unity of hearts and intentions in loyalty to Allah and enmity toward whoever opposes Him, which yields the straightening of rows in prayer, which is the fighting of Satan, and the war, which is the clashing against his party, the people of tyranny, and the actions, which are the fruits of the bodies.

(p. 9) Since staying behind from God's command, and heedlessness toward something whose neglect leads to laxity about it and to failing to observe one of its etiquettes, necessarily results in being in the party of Satan and separated from the party of the All-Merciful, then harming the Messenger (ﷺ) follows, and this necessitates all of that wretchedness, because it is apt to draw one on to something greater than it, until sins envelop a person and calamities become permissible. For reminding through things witnessed and events that occurred, there is an effect that nothing else has in discipline and in the return to warning, He mentioned, as a warning, what happened to the Children of Israel, of a similar kind to their condition, lest one fall into their punishment, when they held back from what they had been commanded concerning the conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House, Jerusalem). God, angered by their deed, named them ﴿fasiqin﴾ (defiantly disobedient) and struck them with al-tih (the wandering in the wilderness) for forty years. In those forty years He caused to die every one of them who had been lax in that matter, so none of them entered Bayt al-Maqdis, and so they were forbidden the lands from which they had held back from conquering them. These lands are Makkah and al-Madinah, the best of God's lands, the emigration place of their forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the dwelling place of his two sons Ishaq and Ya'qub (peace be upon them both), and the purest and most abundant in good and blessing of the lands. This was in addition to the constriction and affliction they were in from the wandering, which is an expulsion from the presence of God, by what He intended, by what the expression of its time as ﴿years﴾ points to, through the evil remembrance and shameful talk they left behind them until the end of time. Then God, Exalted, said: ﴿And when﴾ (as a conjunction) over what its implied meaning is: remember what some of you did, by what I pointed to at the beginning of these verses (p. 10) of etiquettes, from alerting the disbelievers to what may prevent the conquest or be a cause of its difficulty, or the destruction of many people of My servants whom I created in the best of forms, from among the believers and others, or from fleeing from the disbelievers at the clash of battle, or holding back from meeting them when called to it. So that harmed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), whose harm is harm to God, and he bore with you, and accepted, through his abundant mercy toward you and compassion for you, being one of you. The most severe of what his Sender, Glorified is He, rebuked you with was calling you by what is the lowest of the ages in faith, in parallel with His labeling the Children of Israel as ﴿fasiq﴾ with the description that indicates firm entrenchment. Remember when ﴿Musa said to his people﴾, and they, despite being of his own kind, were of those who had the power to do what they were attempting: ﴿O my people﴾, seeking their compassion and urging them toward the pleasure of their Lord, ﴿why do you harm me?﴾, meaning: you renew my harm while persisting in laxity regarding God's command and holding back from the conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis, although I have told you on God's behalf that you will conquer it if you obey Him, and that God swore to your forefathers that He would surely make it yours without doubt.

Since this interrogative of denial necessarily makes one expect what comes after it, namely what necessitates honoring rather than harming, and venerating and submitting rather than hesitating and refusing, he said, confirming the content of the speech with the particle of confirmation: ﴿And indeed﴾, meaning, while the situation is that you ﴿know﴾, meaning you have known with certainty, and this knowledge is renewed for you at every time through the renewal of its causes, through the miracles I have brought you and the Book that preserves you from deviation (p. 11), ﴿that I am the Messenger of God﴾, meaning of the Greatest King, who has no equal, and His Messenger is also to be magnified and honored, not that his majesty is violated or disrespected, ﴿to you﴾. I say nothing to you except from Him, and I do not speak from desire. So disobeying me is disobeying Him, although I have said nothing to you that did not come to pass, and even if you are certain of the opposite, that disobedience is disobedience to Him, with no cause for it at all except the badness of natures.

When he showed compassion toward them, sought their compassion, and reminded them of what they know of his messengership and his connection to God through the signs they witnessed, which are the greatest of favors to them, he knew that they were close to disobedience. So he said, expressing this with the particle ﴿fa﴾ (then), as a consequence of this speech, which is fit to cause steadfastness, and as an immediate sequence and nearness: ﴿So when they deviated﴾, meaning their deviation was realized, close at hand, from God's commands in the Book that came to them, by their refusal to accept His command to advance into the conquest, ﴿God turned their hearts﴾, meaning He who has the whole command, ﴿their hearts﴾ away from uprightness. The plural of multiplicity indicates that only a few of them remained steadfast, so He defeated them before their enemies and struck them with the wandering, because they defied God's command. [So God] does not guide them. He attributed the sin to them and the punishment to Himself, although all of it is from Him, in order to teach His servants etiquette and to inform them that their voluntary acts are ascribed to them as their acquisition, and that the proof stands against them because they did not know the outcome. ﴿And God﴾, meaning the Greatest King, to whom belongs perfect wisdom, since He combines the attributes of perfection, (p. 12) ﴿does not guide﴾, meaning with the guidance of success after the guidance of clarification, ﴿the defiant people﴾, meaning those who are the two extremes in defiance, who had the power to attempt, yet weakness did not hold them back from defiance. So beware of being like them in resolve, lest you equal them in the penalties for crimes. Ended.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 61, verse 6 (part 1 of 3):

Since the harm done to the Prophet ﷺ by disobeying his command sometimes occurs together with knowledge of his prophethood and acknowledgment of it, and sometimes together with denial, he first addressed the reproach for what came from them on the assumption of acceptance. In it he reminded them of the story of Musa, peace be upon him, whom they harmed while knowing of his prophethood, and he warned them with what befell them of the deviation of hearts, which are the pillar of bodies and the soundness of the human being. Then he followed this with what happens from him (ﷺ) when denial is assumed. Since refuting denial is sometimes done by reason and sometimes by transmitted text, and what is done by reason is through observing miracles, especially the bringing forth of what was hidden (al-khaba'), which happened to him (ﷺ) in the story of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him, when his letter was brought out, which he had striven to conceal and which the riding woman carrying it had striven to hide, there is in that a convincing proof of knowledge of the prophethood and of the certainty of his exalted status. He followed that with a transmitted proof in support of reason, and it is also a proof of the truthfulness of the report concerning the turning away of the hearts of the Children of Israel as a recompense for their deviation from the truth. So He said: ﴿And when﴾, that is, remember when, ﴿Isa said﴾, and He described him with what established who he was, so He said: ﴿son of Maryam﴾, that is, to the people of Musa, peace be upon them both, to whom he was sent, and whose acceptance of his prophethood was established among them by miracles, along with his sincere call to Allah and his confirmation of those among the people of Allah who came before him: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾. He reminded them of the religion their father had followed and of what he enjoined upon his son of adherence to Islam. He did not address them as "people" as Musa, peace be upon him, had said, because he has no father among them, even though his mother is from among them, for lineage is only through the father. He emphasized it against the denial of some of them, so He said: ﴿Indeed I am the messenger of Allah﴾, that is, of the King, the Greatest, whose knowledge encompasses everything, ﴿to you﴾, that is, not to others, while I am ﴿confirming﴾ (musaddiqan). It is in the accusative because of what is in "messenger" of the sense of a verb, and it is not governed by "to you," because it is a description of the messenger. Prepositions do not govern by themselves, but by the sense of a verb within them. So when they are relational particles (silat) that do not contain the meaning of a verb, they do not govern. This is the particle which is called, outside the Noble Book, "superfluous" (laghw). ﴿of what is before me﴾, that is, it precedes me and existed before me, ﴿of the Torah﴾, which you know Allah sent down to Musa, peace be upon him, and which is the first of the books revealed after the scrolls (suhuf), and by which the prophets judged. So my confirmation of it, together with my support for it, is a supporter, because the proofs I have established are true, and it makes clear that it is my evidence in what I have not abrogated from it, just as a person is guided by the landmarks before him and watches them with his sight.

When he mentioned the first of the books, he also mentioned the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in being sent, who is the last of the messengers, so that this would be an indication that the good news of him is in the Torah and the Gospel. So He said: ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾, that is, while I confirm the Torah.

Since his message (ﷺ) was general for all creation, he did not mention a limiting particle (harf al-ghayah) in his message as he did in the two messages mentioned before. So He said: ﴿with a messenger﴾, that is, to everyone who is included in lordship (al-marbubiyyah), ﴿who will come﴾. Since his coming would be after a long period, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after me﴾. Since the coming with the utmost clarity and removal of confusion in every respect is more effective in rebuking those who fall short after him and in seizing those who transgress and break his covenant, He brought the name which no one shared with the Prophet (ﷺ) in his time or before him at all, and its pattern indicates intensification of its meaning. So He said: ﴿his name is Ahmad﴾, that is, it indicates that he is the most eloquent of creation in praising and being praised, and this is his name (ﷺ) in the heaven to which this bringer of good news will return. In singling out his mention there is a precaution against the assumption that the Prophet is distant in rank, because it hints, by beginning with the hamza, which is the first of the letters in articulation and the strongest of the throat letters, which is the first of the places of articulation, and by including the mim, that he (ﷺ), just as he is the Seal, is indicated by his most famous and greatest name "Muhammad," since it begins with the mim, which is the most accessible of the lip letters, and the lip letters are the conclusion of the letters, because their point of articulation is the last of the points of articulation. He is the one who comes first in position in mention, nobility and judgment by the noble description, that is, there is no prophet before him in creation, and prophethood was obligatory for him while Adam was still lying in his clay. Between the spirit and the body, as is in the hadith which Ahmad recorded from Maysara al-Fajr, may Allah be pleased with him, and al-Tirmidhi recorded from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it at the beginning of the Proofs of Prophethood, and he said: its meaning is that this is so in the decree and determination of Allah. It seems he means a decree written in the Mother of the Book and mentioned to whoever He willed among the angels before the completion of the creation of Adam, peace be upon him. For it is possible that when He, glorified and exalted, formed Adam, peace be upon him, He made his clay translucent through which his descendants could be seen, and He made for the righteous among them a light visible apart from others. When they saw the greatest of them in light, they asked about him, and He, glorified and exalted, informed them about him and recorded what He willed of his attributes in the Mother of the Book. Likewise he was a prophet through the report in the supplication of his father Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and through the good news of Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, and through the signs of the light which came out of his mother, as in the hadith which al-Bayhaqi and others narrated in the Proofs from al-'Irbad ibn Sariya, may Allah be pleased with him: "Indeed I am the servant of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets." In another narration: "Indeed I am the servant of Allah for the Seal of the Prophets, and [indeed] Adam was lying in his clay, and I will inform you of that: the supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of Isa concerning me, and the vision my mother saw," and likewise the mothers of the prophets see such things. And the mother of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw, when she gave birth to him, a light which lit up for her the palaces of Syria. So the interpretation of that by His mentioning him to His angels is like its interpretation as the supplication of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in His saying, quoting him: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among them who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129]. And the good news of Isa, peace be upon him, is like his report in this verse, and its interpretation by the light which his mother saw is like its interpretation by the light which the angels, peace be upon them, may have seen in the translucent clay of Adam, peace be upon him. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Surah Muhammad was more worthy of his name, which indicates sealing, because sealing needs repair to mend what has split in separation. Likewise surah al-Fath, because of what it requires of attempting what is closed and removing closure. The ending of both surahs with the mim is of great relevance to that, because the mim is a name for the completion of the outward (al-zahir), standing with the alif, and to this points the writing of the alif of tanwin in al-Fath after the mim, together with the fact that it does not lack an indication that he is the Opener while also being the Seal. This is supported by the opening of the surah with the first letter of the name which is pleasing (al-malih) for victory (al-fath). And this surah was more worthy of it, because it is the most indicative sign of agreement and unity of word without disagreement and division, as it was at the descent of Adam, peace be upon him, and after him for a period. To this he pointed by its ending and the ending of its counterpart al-Saffat with the nun, which is a manifest, clarifying, encompassing manifestation of what it displays. So it gives good news to this community of gathering and dominance upon the name whose last part encompasses all the people of the earth in the time of the bringer of good news, Isa, peace be upon him, who confirms the one given good news by renewing his command and establishing his religion (ﷺ). The end of this is the result of the end of al-Saffat with praise, which is the encompassing of the attributes of perfection. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best what is correct.

(p-١٨) Mention of what confirms this verse from the Gospel regarding its confirmation of the Torah.

And His giving good news of Ahmad (ﷺ). He said: There was a sick man named al-'Azar (Lazarus) from Bayt 'Anya (Bethany), who was the brother of Maryam (Mary) and Marta (Martha). The two sisters sent to Yasu' (Jesus), saying that the one whom he loves is sick. He remained in the place where he was for two days. Then he said to his disciples: "Let us go to Judea." His disciples said to him: "Just now, Teacher, the Jews wanted to stone you, and you want to go back to them?" He said: "Our beloved al-'Azar has fallen asleep, but I will go and wake him." They said: "Our master, if he is sleeping, he will awaken." Then he said: "al-'Azar has died." So they came to Bayt 'Anya, and he had been in the tomb for four days. Bayt 'Anya was about fifteen ghalwas (a ghalwa is a unit of distance, roughly a bowshot) from Yarushalim (Jerusalem). Many of the Jews had come to Marta and Maryam to console them. When Marta heard of Yasu's coming, she went out to meet him and said to him: "Master, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But I know that God will give you whatever you ask of Him." He said: "Your brother will rise." She said: "I know that he will rise in the Resurrection." Then Maryam came to meet him (p-19), and the Jews who were consoling her thought that she was going to the tomb, so they followed her. When she reached the place where Yasu' was, she fell down prostrate at his feet. When he saw her weeping, and the Jews who were with her, he said: "Where have you laid him?" They said to him: "Master, come and see." Yasu' wept. The Jews said: "See how he loved him!" Some of them said: "Could not this one who opened the eyes of the blind have caused this one not to die?" He came to the tomb, which was a cave with a stone placed upon it, and said: "Remove the stone." Marta, the dead man's sister, said to him: "Master, he has already begun to stink, for he has been dead four days." Yasu' said to her: "Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?" They removed the stone. Yasu' lifted his eyes upward and said: "I thank You, for You hear me. I say this for the sake of this crowd, so that they may believe that You sent me." Having said this, he called out with a loud voice and cried: "al-'Azar, come out!" The dead man came out, his hands and feet bound with grave-cloths, and his face wrapped in a turban. Yasu' said: "Untie him and let him go." Many of the Jews who had come to Maryam, when they saw what Yasu' had done, believed. But some of them went to the Pharisees and informed them. The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said: "What shall we do, since this man performs many signs? If we leave him, all people will believe in him, and the Romans will come and overthrow (p-20) our nation and our place." One of them, named Qayafa (Caiaphas), who was the high priest that year, said to them: "It is better for us that one man of the people die rather than the whole nation perish," and so on, to the end of what has passed in al-Nisa' at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ [al-Nisa': 157], the verses. We return to the point. He said: Then the Pharisees went away and conspired to trap him with a word, so they sent to him their disciples and the Herodians, saying: "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not care about anyone, nor do you look at the face of a person. So tell us what you think: is it lawful for us to pay the poll-tax to Caesar or not?" Yasu' perceived their malice and said: "Why do you test me, hypocrites? Show me the coin of the tax." They brought him a denarius. He said to them: "Whose image and inscription is this?" They said: "Caesar's." Then he said to them: "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." When they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away. John said: Yasu' said: "I will remain with you a short time, then I will go to Him who sent me, and you will seek me but will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come." (p-21) The Jews said among themselves: "Where is this one about to go, that we will not find him? Is he about to go to the dispersion of the Greeks?" Matthew said: On that day, the heretics who say there is no resurrection came to him and asked him, and he mentioned their question and his answer to them, until he said at the end of his answer: "Have you not read what was said to you by God?" Mark said: In the Book of Moses, God's word at the bush, when He said: "I am the God of Ibrahim (Abraham), the God of Ishaq (Isaac), and the God of Ya'qub (Jacob)," and you go greatly astray. The wording of Luke: Moses indicated this at the bush, as the Lord said: "I am the God of Ibrahim, the God of Ishaq, and the God of Ya'qub." Matthew said: When the crowd heard, they were astonished at his teaching. When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the heretics, they gathered together against him, and one of their scholars asked him to test him, saying: "Teacher, which commandment is greatest in the Nomos (the Law)?" Yasu' said to him: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart." And he said: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one; you shall love your God with all your heart," (end), "and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second, which is like it, is that you love your neighbor as yourself." Mark said: "There is no commandment greater than these two" (end). On these two commandments depend the whole Nomos and the Prophets. Mark said: The scholar said to him: "Then, Teacher of truth, I say that He is one, and there is none other than Him, and that one must love Him with all the heart, (p-22) and with all the intention, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and love your neighbor as yourself. This is better than all the sacrifices and burnt offerings." When Yasu' saw his understanding, he answered him, saying: "You are not far from the Kingdom of God." Luke said: He said to Yasu': "And who is my neighbor?" Yasu' said: "A man was going down from Yarushalim to Ariha (Jericho), and he fell among robbers, who stripped him and wounded him and went away, leaving him half-dead. It happened that a priest came down that road, and saw him and passed by. Likewise a Levite came to the place, saw him and passed by. But a Samaritan passed by him; when he saw him, he was moved with compassion, approached him, bound his wounds, lifted him onto his own animal, brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said: 'Look after him, and if you spend more than these two, I will repay you when I return.' Which of these three do you think became a neighbor to the one who fell among the robbers?" He said: "The one who showed him mercy." Yasu' said to him: "Go and do likewise." Mark said: No one dared to ask him further. Then he said: A large crowd was listening to him eagerly. John said: Many believed in his name when he was in Irushalim during the feast of Passover, because they had witnessed the signs that he performed. Then he said: There was a man of the Pharisees named Nayqudimis (Nicodemus), a ruler of the Jews, who came to Yasu' by night and said to him: "[O] Teacher, (p-23) we know that you have come from God as a teacher, for no one is able to perform these signs that you perform unless God is with him." Matthew said: Then Yasu' addressed the crowd and his disciples, and said: "The scribes and the Pharisees sit on the seat of Moses. So whatever they tell you, observe and do, but do not imitate their deeds, for they say and do not do. They bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with a finger. All their deeds they do to be seen by people; they display their garments and enlarge the hems of their clothes, they love the first places at feasts, the chief seats in the synagogues, the greetings in the markets, and to be called teachers by people. But as for you, do not call anyone a teacher on earth, nor a leader, for your leader is one, the Messiah, and you are all brothers. Do not call anyone on earth your father, for your Father is one, He who is in the heavens. The greatest among you shall be your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you devour the houses of widows and orphans, under pretense of long prayers; therefore you will receive greater judgment. Woe to you, for you shut the Kingdom of Heaven before people; you do not enter, nor do you let those who wish to enter go in. Woe to you, for you traverse land and sea to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a child of Gehenna as yourselves. Woe to you, blind guides, you who say: 'Whoever swears by the Temple, it is nothing, but whoever swears by the gold of the Temple is bound.' (p-24) Blind fools, which is greater: the gold, or the Temple that sanctifies the gold? And whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the offering that is upon it is bound. Blind fools, which is greater: the offering, or the altar that sanctifies the offering? Whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by all that is upon it; whoever swears by the Temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it; whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits upon it. Woe to you, for you tithe mint, dill and cumin, and neglect the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy and faith." Luke said: "You tithe mint, rue and every herb, and reject God's justice and His love. These you ought to have done without neglecting those" (end). O guides of 'Ayman (Sinai?), who leave the gnat and swallow the camel! Woe to you, for you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, while their inside is full of plunder and injustice. Blind one, cleanse first the inside of the cup and the dish so that their outside may become clean. Luke said: "Give alms, and all things will be clean for you." Woe to you, for you are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful outside but inside are full of the bones of the dead and every impurity. Luke said: "For you are like hidden graves, and people walk over them without knowing" (end).
Likewise you appear to people as righteous outwardly, but inwardly you are full of sin and hypocrisy. Luke said: "And you, scribes, woe to you, for you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves will not lift them with one of your fingers. Woe to you, for you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter, and you hindered those who wished to enter" (end). Woe to you, for you build the tombs of the prophets. Luke said: "whom your fathers killed" (end), and you adorn the sepulchres of the righteous and say: "If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have shared with them in the blood of the prophets." Thus you bear witness against yourselves that you are sons of the murderers of the prophets. Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers. Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna? Therefore I send to you prophets, wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and "pursue" from city to city, so that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth. Luke said: "And you bear witness and approve the deeds of your fathers, for they killed them, and you build their tombs. Therefore the wisdom of God said: 'Behold, I will send to them prophets and apostles, and they will kill some of them and persecute them, so that the blood of all the prophets shed from the beginning of the world may be avenged upon this generation.'"

Matthew said: "From the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar. Truly I say to you [that] all this will come upon this generation. O Jerusalem, O killer of the prophets and stoner of those sent to her! How many times [you wanted] that I gather your children within you, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you did not want to. Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I say to you: you will not see me from now until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

Mark said: "Then Jesus came to the door of the treasury and watched the crowd putting copper into the treasury, and many rich people put in much. A poor widow came and put in two mites. He called his disciples and said to them: Truly I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who put into the treasury, for they all put in from their surplus, but she put in from her poverty all that she had. Then he went out of the Temple." End of quotation.

This is what contains the evidence for the mission and the confirmation of the Torah (al-Tawrah). As for the good tidings of Muhammad ﷺ, they have already been discussed in this book, dispersed across the surahs such as al-A'raf, al-Nisa' and others.

Ibn Hisham said in his abridgement of the Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, the compilation of Ibn Ishaq: Ibn Ishaq said: "It has reached me that the description of the Messenger of God ﷺ was, among what God the Exalted revealed to Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both, in the Gospel (al-Injil) for the people of the Gospel, from the attributes of the Messenger of God ﷺ, which Yahnas the disciple (al-Hawari) affirmed for them when he copied out the Gospel for them from the time of Jesus son of Mary [concerning] the Messenger of God ﷺ, to them, that he said: 'Whoever hates me hates the Lord. Had I not performed among them deeds that no one before me had performed, they would have had no sin. But now they have become insolent and thought that they would overpower me, and also the Lord. But the word that is in the Law (al-Namus) must be fulfilled: they hated me without cause, i.e. in vain. So when the Manhamana comes, whom God sends to you from the Lord, the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus), who proceeds from the Lord, he will bear witness concerning me, and you also, because from the beginning you have been with me. I have told you this so that you will not doubt.'" Thus, "al-Manhamana" in Syriac is Muhammad ﷺ, and in Greek (al-Rumiyyah) it is "al-Barqalitus" (the Paraclete). End of quotation.

When the textual proof for the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ was complete, and for his being the noblest of the prophets, opening their line and sealing it, it indicated the binding of the Children of Israel to their deviation. So He said: ﴿So when [Jesus or Muhammad] came to them, the Children of Israel and others, with clear proofs﴾, i.e. the great miracles which no sensible person can refuse but to accept, and the Manifest Book, ﴿they said﴾, i.e. at the time of its coming, whether without any consideration or reflection, ﴿"This"﴾, i.e. what was brought of the clear proofs, or the one who brought them, in exaggeration, as indicated by the reading of Hamzah, ﴿"is sorcery"﴾ (the particle "fa" in "fa-lamma" indicates immediacy, showing how closely disbelief was attached to the very first moments of the coming). They were the first to disbelieve in him, because this is an attribute necessarily belonging to them, whether it reached them while they were alone or with others joined to them. ﴿"Manifest"﴾, i.e. clear in its sorcery, to the extent that its very manifestness to everyone who saw it was that it is sorcery, out of obstinacy and arrogance on their part toward the truth, which has no confusion in it.

When the implied meaning was "a declaration that they are the most unjust of people, because of their deliberate lying," then "Who is more unjust" is coordinated with it, in the sense of "who is more unjust than them, because of their shamelessness in that." He generalizes it to include everyone who has their attribute, saying: ﴿who fabricates against God﴾, that is, deliberately attributes to ﴿God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿falsehood﴾, which is the ugliest of things. ﴿And he is﴾, that is, while the state is that he ﴿is being called﴾, that is, by whatever caller, ﴿to Islam﴾, which is the best of things. So a slight reminder is enough in calling to it, because it is acknowledging the truth to the one who is entitled to it. Thus, in place of the response, fabricating a lie is put in ﴿that state﴾, the best state.

When the implied meaning was: "then God does not guide him because of his injustice," then "God" is coordinated with it, that is, the One to whom all command belongs, so there is no command for anyone alongside Him. ﴿Does not guide the people﴾, that is, does not create guidance in the hearts of those among whom is the strength to strive against difficult matters, ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who stumble in their minds the way one stumbles who is in darkness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 61, verse 8:

When He had informed of their rejection of the message, He gave its cause in His saying: ﴿They desire﴾, meaning they bring about the desire to reject the message through their fabrication, ﴿to extinguish﴾, meaning in order that they may extinguish ﴿the light of Allah﴾, meaning the King to whom nothing is comparable, ﴿with their mouths﴾, meaning with what they say of falsehood, which has no source other than the mouths, because it has no belief in the hearts, since no intelligent person could imagine it. They are, in this, like those who blow at the sun, desiring that their blowing might wipe out its disc and that their blemish might diminish its adornment. Thus He likened their desire to hide the Qur'an, through their denial and all their scheming, to one who desires to extinguish the sun by blowing on it, and he is in the most exhausting and most misguided error:

؎And in the toil of one who envies the sun its light ∗∗∗ and strives to reach it with a blow

This therefore indicates the restriction of the verb: all their desire is directed toward this aim, they have no desire other than that, and it is not fitting that they should have a desire, because they are slaves, and desire is fitting only for the master, so that the slave's desire follows his, and thus becomes obedience to his desire. So it is as if he had no desire at all. This is more eloquent than what is in Bara'a, because this is its outcome.

When He had informed of the cause of their desire and alluded to it, which is their command after He had informed of their rejection of the truth and emboldened Himself against them by informing of their misguidance, He increased that by His saying, mentioning explicitly rather than by pronoun, to draw attention to [all] the attributes of majesty and honour: ﴿and Allah﴾, meaning the One for whom there is no repeller, [for Him] because of the completeness of His greatness. And since this surah is the outcome of the surah of Bara'a, in which He informed that He refuses except to complete His light, He informed in this one of the outcome of that, which is the permanence and continuance of the completion of the light, because this is the manner of the King to whom there is no equal: when He wills a thing, how much more when He sends a messenger. So He said: ﴿completing﴾. This meaning supports the view of the majority [that it] is Medinan after the strengthening, by mention of jihad, for its prescription was after the Hijra from ... And the apparent [order] from its arrangement after the Mumtahana, which was revealed concerning the Conquest expedition, is that it is after Bara'a in revelation as well.

Since the light, for the manifestation of the forms of things after their obliteration, is a cause for placing things in their most perfect positions, and since what came from Allah of knowledge was likewise, its essence was made light, and so its name was applied to it, and He said: ﴿His light﴾. Therefore, the concealment of it by anyone through denial of it or the desire to extinguish it does not harm it. He increased that by His saying: ﴿even if the disbelievers dislike it﴾, meaning the completion of it [for them], ﴿the disbelievers﴾, meaning those firmly rooted in the attribute of disbelief, striving in defending against it.

When he had informed of that, he gave the reason with what is the way of every king, so how much more so with the One who is unique in His dominion. He said: ﴿He it is﴾, that is, the One whose attributes of beauty and majesty are established as comprehensive, He alone, without having any partner or minister, ﴿who sent﴾ by what He has of power and will, ﴿His Messenger﴾, that is, the one deserving that everyone who receives his message should honour him, because his greatness derives from the greatness of the One who sent him. The particle of limit (ḥarf al-ghāya) is not mentioned, as an indication of the generality of the sending to everyone whom the kingdom encompasses, as has passed. ﴿With guidance﴾, that is, the sufficient clarification, ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, that is, the kingdom whose firmness is not approached by any firmness, so there is no firmness for anything else; the firmness of this religion is by His firmness. It is also possible that the meaning is: and the religion which is the truth, established in its truthfulness, perfect in it with a perfection that belongs to no other. In that case it is an idāfa of the qualified to its quality, indicating the intensity of its attachment to it. ﴿That He may make it prevail﴾, that is, raise it up (p-32) along with fame and the humiliation of the opponent, ﴿over the religion﴾, that is, the genus of the sharia which lays down what it legislates of rulings, by which it rewards whoever follows it and whoever deviates from it, ﴿all of it﴾, so no religion remains except that it is beneath it, is annihilated by it, and its adherents are humbled before it with a humiliation not comparable to any other humiliation. ﴿Even if the polytheists dislike it﴾, that is, its manifestation, ﴿the polytheists﴾, that is, those obstinate in their disbelief, firmly persisting in that obstinacy. The greatest target of this are the people of obstinacy with the innovation of unity (ittiḥād, the doctrine of the unity of existence), for they have left nothing that is other than Him without associating it with Him, exalted is God above what they say, a great exaltation. They, despite the remoteness of their creed from sound reason and the corruption of it from imaginings, and its collision with all the transmitted texts, are extremely numerous, because people have come to what God and His Messenger promised [and God and His Messenger spoke truly], that most of them would have their covenants corrupted, their trusts hidden, and would become refuse like the refuse of dates, of no account to God. Yet they, despite their numbers, by what this verse and its like contain, are in extreme humiliation, and to God be praise, they have no honour except by displaying adherence to the Book and the Sunna. They know that they lie in this claim, because they are in extreme opposition to both, to the point that they believe both to be polytheism, since both establish for God the Exalted an existence differing from the existence of creation. They say, out of obstinacy against what is necessarily known, that existence is one, and that there is no existent, apparent or hidden, other than Him; for this reason they named existence by Him. Then their knowledge of their own abasement, and that they have no honour except (p-33) within the protection of the sharia, does not turn them back from their error. So I marvel at that, and I resort to God the Exalted, asking for well-being, for hearts are in the hand of God, He turns them however He wills. And His striking them with humiliation despite their numbers is in extreme indication of God, glorified is He, because a perfectly powerful King does not allow one who impugns His dominion and strives to reject His message and to humiliate His messengers. Indeed He, glorified is He, has fulfilled much of what He promised him, with what indicates—since it is a dominance over the most powerful of kings, the Chosroes and the Caesars—power over the rest. That is because when his people held back from supporting him, and hastened to deny him and rejected what they had witnessed of his truthfulness, God facilitated for him helpers from his community: the stalwarts of the tribes, the excellent among the virtuous, and the masters among the noble, and they reached the furthest of hopes in supporting him.

When this whole matter produced its result, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was made victorious in every circumstance, and the ruin of whoever opposes his command came about. It necessarily followed that jihad with him is a profitable trade, because victory is guaranteed, and death is a watering place that one must reach, whether a person plunges into dangers or guards himself in lofty fortresses. So God, exalted is He, said, in the style of address and interrogation, because it is more majestic and more stirring, with the particle after which nothing but the utmost in greatness can follow: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, who have said in their profession of faith, and what is incumbent upon them is to act in accordance with its requirements, ﴿Shall I direct you﴾, while I am the One who encompasses all in knowledge and power. It is therefore a command in meaning, expressed in the form of a question to stir the soul, so that it falls more forcefully upon the self and is more readily accepted by it. The verse is also a consequence of what preceded, from another standpoint: when He rebuked them for the dissolving of resolve, informed them of what fighting requires, and reproached them for opposing the Messenger ﷺ, and informed them that whoever opposes him harms only himself, the place of racing to obedience was reached. So He arranged upon this the longing to hear of its fruit, and He mentioned it. And since the deed of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him, was for the sake of the fact that his family, who were in Makkah, would not be saved, neither in their persons nor in any of their property, and this was in the sense of trade, He said: ﴿upon a trade﴾. The recitation of Ibn 'Amir ﴿tunjikum﴾ with the doubled letter is more suitable to this context than the recitation of the majority with the single letter, while the recitation of the majority is more suitable to the aim of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿from a painful punishment﴾, through the loss of self or property.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 61, verse 11:

Since trade (ittijar) is the exertion of the self in obtaining beneficial profit, and since faith (iman) and jihad are the greatest exertion of the self in securing [the everlasting Garden] (al-jannah al-baqiyah), for which no commodity is an equivalent, He borrowed for them the name of that trade. The response to a call (nida') is coming forward (iqbal), and the response to a question (istifham) is "yes" (na'am). So they are addressed as though they had come forward and said yes, as an alert to what is most fitting for them. He then began to explain the trade: it is the combining of faith, which is the foundation of all deeds, and jihad in both its forms, the one that perfects the self and the one that perfects others. So He said: ﴿You believe﴾, meaning, "Believe" [(ay) amanu], on the condition of renewing faith continually, ﴿in Allah﴾, who possesses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, whose confirmation is the sign of inward submission and humility, by virtue of his being a king. ﴿And strive﴾, meaning, "Strive," as a demonstration of the soundness of your faith, through renewal and continuity.

That these two verbs carry the sense of a command is indicated by the jussive (jazm) form of what is placed in the position of the answer, together with the qira'ah (recitation variant) of Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him: "Believe and strive" in the imperative form. ﴿In the way of Allah﴾, meaning, by means of facilitating the path of the Greatest King, which leads to Him, whose command belongs to no one else. This makes it a container for you in [all] of this action, so that nothing of it falls outside of it, so that it is pure, by conquering the land of the Hajj, so that access to it becomes easy for everyone who wishes it, and other than that of His laws. Thus you will be among those whose deed confirms their word. This meaning is free of any difficulty, because there is a distinction between our saying "So-and-so did such-and-such," which is true of a single occurrence, and our saying "by his doing," which indicates that his doing has become a habit for him. So the meaning is: O you who have done faith, if you desire salvation, then be deeply rooted in the description of faith, truly committed to it, firm in its advance, and persevere in jihad as evidence of that. For jihad, with the danger, hardship and harm it entails, is the greatest proof of the truthfulness of faith. This is supported by the fact that the context concerns the story of Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him, which apparently suggests a lack of steadfastness in faith and a desire for jihad, which points to the one who is truthful in it. For this reason Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said what he said. And Allah is the Guide.

Since combining the soul and its equivalent, wealth, in a manner of willingness and desire, is more indicative of the soundness of faith, He said: ﴿with your wealth﴾, and He put it first because of its value in that time, and because it is the sustenance of souls and bodies. Whoever spends all his wealth will not withhold his soul, because wealth sustains it. When He mentioned the sustainer first, He followed it with what it sustains, saying: ﴿and your lives﴾. Since He commanded this in the form of a statement, for emphasis and to affirm its importance, He pointed to its greatness by praising it before mentioning its reward. So He said: ﴿That﴾, meaning, this great matter of faith and its confirmation through jihad, ﴿is better for you﴾, meaning, specifically better for you than what you desire of vacillation through advising the disbelievers, ﴿if you know﴾, meaning, if it is possible for knowledge to be renewed in you at any time, then you know that this is better for you. When you know that it is better, you will turn towards it, and it will have great significance for you. But if your hearts have been so thoroughly sealed that there is no hope for their reform, then pray over yourselves the prayer of the dead (salat al-mawt).

When the meaning of "*tu'minun*" (you believe) was: the matter is as previously mentioned, but it has been turned away from that to what has been mentioned. The thing most important to a person is his fear of what he has been threatened with, so He, glorified is He, secured them from that, indicating the root of the action by putting in the jussive (*jazm*) form what stands in the position of the answer (*jawab*), and said: ﴿He will forgive you﴾, that is, specifically, unlike those who did not do that, ﴿your sins﴾, that is, by erasing their substances and all their traces.

When He had struck the hearts with the bitterness of punishment and reproach, He gave them pleasure with the goodness of reward, and said: ﴿and admit you﴾, that is, after purifying you by forgiveness, out of mercy for you, ﴿to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. The phrase indicates the nearness of the flowing water and its winding through the lands by the prepositional phrase, so He said: ﴿beneath them﴾, that is, beneath their trees, their chambers, and every place of recreation in them, ﴿the rivers﴾. Thus they are always fresh and blossoming. This style did not need mention of eternal abiding (*khulud*), since what follows it suffices without it. It indicated the excessive abundance in the circuit by His words in the form of the highest plural: ﴿and dwellings﴾. And since dwellings are not pleasing except by the good meanings that accompany them, He said: ﴿good﴾, that is, in spaciousness, the variety of (p-38) kinds of delights, the height of buildings and couches, together with ease of access to them, the beauty of views, and the easy passage of breezes through the spacious buildings, along with the goodness of the chambers. The water flowing beneath them did not spoil any of their fragrance, nor their temperateness, in any respect of what is desired from them. And since no one desires them except for lasting residence, He clarified their suitability for that by His words: ﴿in gardens of Eden﴾, that is, orchards fit for dwelling in them, requiring no outside thing for their upkeep, which would require going out of them to obtain it, and having no end to that dwelling. Hamza al-Karmani said in his book *Jawami' al-Tafsir*: it is the capital (*qasabah*) of the gardens, and the city of Paradise, nearest of them to the Throne.

When this was a noble matter not found in anything else, He said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the very great matter alone, ﴿is the great triumph﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 61, verse 13:

When he had mentioned what He had bestowed upon them in the other (blessing), because it is more important for its permanence, the implied sense, indicated by the conjunction (ʿaṭf), was: "This is for you, and [there is] another (blessing) conjoined to it, which He has made for them in this world." So he said: ﴿and another [blessing]﴾, meaning: "and for you there is another blessing," or "He will give you," or "He will increase you in another blessing." Since man loves most what is immediate and rejoices most in what is at hand, he said: ﴿you love it﴾, meaning with a great love, continually renewed (p-39) and increasing. Thus in the outward sense of this good news there is an enticement to jihad and an endearing of it, and in its inward sense there is an exhortation toward [love of] martyrdom, along with what it indicates of rebuke for preferring the immediate and a reproach: ﴿a help from Allah﴾, meaning He whose greatness encompasses everything, and in proportion to His encompassing will be His help for you; ﴿and a near victory﴾, meaning you will enter through it into every matter that had been difficult for you, from the fortresses of your enemies and other of their affairs, during the life of your Prophet ﷺ, the greatest of which is the conquest of Makkah, concerning which Ḥāṭib (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) wrote what he wrote, and after his death. In this there is a testimony for Ḥāṭib (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) that he loves the victory of the Prophet ﷺ and the conquest of Makkah and other places for him, because of the soundness of his faith, as the Prophet ﷺ, who does not speak from desire, informed.

Since the preceding reproach was a warning to those whose actions contradicted their words among those who believed, and the context had taken its share of warning and rebuke, he omitted what its implied sense is: "So He warned those among the hypocrites who were not firmly rooted in the religion, and those among the believers whose actions contradicted their words." He followed it, as an indication of it, so that it would have a stronger effect on the soul for those to whom its omission alludes, by way of appeal: ﴿And give good news to the believers﴾, meaning those for whom faith has become a firmly established attribute, like Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Balta'ah (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu): that Allah will open for you the lands east and west, and the first of that is the honored city of Makkah. And He does not oblige them (p-40) to defend their clans and their wealth, nor that any of their actions should contradict any of their words.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 61, verse 14:

When Allah, glorified is He, stirred them toward jihad and made them eager for it by describing it as a profitable trade, and hinted at warning through encouragement by good tidings, the souls became prepared to turn toward it and were moved to a full response. He urged them to it with an affirmation that implies reward or punishment. So He said, calling out with the particle of distance and with an expression that indicates the lowest degree, as a rebuke, to show that the attribute of faith is not lost except when it is joined with deprivation, in order to arouse eagerness and affection: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ [i.e., affirm this, and submit to this admonition with the utmost submission]: indeed I have commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to say to you: ﴿Be﴾ [i.e., with the utmost of your effort] ﴿helpers of Allah﴾ [i.e., firmly established in the attribute of helping, at the highest summit of steadfastness of feet in supporting the One who has absolute self-sufficiency], so that you may be, by what the reading of the community (al-jama'ah) indicates through the idafah (construct form), through striving in that, as if you were all His helpers. For you are more noble than the people of Jesus, peace be upon him, and He, glorified is He, did not call you to His support except to honor you by companionship with His messengers, who are the essence of His creation, peace be upon them. So say: ﴿We have heard and we obey﴾ [we are the helpers of Allah]. Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read with tanwin and the lam of genitive, meaning: be some of His helpers. It seems that what is commanded in this reading is steadfastness in (p-41) faith, even at the lowest of its degrees, while in the reading of the majority it is firm rootedness in it.

Since the intended meaning was a quality which, in steadfastness and swiftness, is like the quality of the Hawariyyun (the disciples of Jesus), He expressed this with His words: ﴿as﴾ [i.e., be for my sake, since I have called you with my word without intermediary, and have delighted you with my address], just as the Hawariyyun were the helpers of Allah when ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said﴾ [when I sent him to the Children of Israel, abrogating the law of Musa, peace be upon him] ﴿to the Hawariyyun﴾ [i.e., the pure and special companions from among them]: ﴿Who are my helpers﴾ [while they are traveling in the stations of conduct and dealings, and the stages of striving and encounters] ﴿toward Allah﴾ [i.e., the One who encompasses everything, so to Him we return just as we originated from Him].

When the listener's longing for their answer grew intense, He clarified it with His words: ﴿The Hawariyyun said﴾ [informing that they were utterly earnest in this with no further degree beyond it, acting in what they were called to as one who has arrived, not as one who is still traveling], [knowing that his call is the call of Allah, for he does not speak from desire; so his speech is nothing but from Allah]: ﴿We﴾ [all of us together] ﴿are the helpers of Allah﴾ [i.e., the Supreme King who is free of need of us and able to complete our support; even if the enemy were all the people of the earth, we would support Him now in deed, needing no slight training, and looking to nothing but our keeping in mind all that a human being can grasp of His attributes of majesty, beauty and perfection]. For this reason they declared it openly and did not conceal it.

Since the intended meaning was: then they called to those among the Children of Israel who opposed them, and fought them (p-42), this was caused by His words: ﴿So a group﴾ [i.e., people among them who have the capacity for turning around, because of their great number] ﴿of the Children of Israel believed﴾ [i.e., in him, the people of his nation] ﴿and a group disbelieved﴾ [i.e., from among them]. The original meaning of ta'ifah is a piece of a thing. ﴿So We strengthened﴾ [i.e., We empowered, after the raising of Jesus, peace be upon him] ﴿those who believed﴾ [i.e., those who affirmed sincere faith among them and others, in word and deed], and We strengthened their hearts ﴿against their enemy﴾ [those who opposed them for the sake of their faith]. Since the attainment of what is beloved is most beloved when it comes at the beginning of the day, His support is consequently described by His words: ﴿So they became dominant﴾ [i.e., they became, after the humiliation they had been in, high, victorious and overpowering in their words and deeds, fearing no one except Allah and not finding themselves weak before Him]. Support is sometimes through knowledge and sometimes through action: ﴿He was taught by one of mighty powers﴾ [al-Najm: 5], so His knowledge became in the utmost firmness, and a power followed it that is at the furthest limit of perfection, because it arises from knowledge acquired through power; otherwise it would have said: "His knowledge is great knowledge." ﴿He who had knowledge from the Book said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾ [al-Naml: 40] is a power acquired from knowledge. The apparent meaning, as is apparent from His exalted words: ﴿And those who follow you above those who disbelieved, until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55], and other verses, is that the support of the believers [through him] came shortly after his raising, when the Hawariyyun appeared and spread through the lands calling to Allah with the signs He had given them, and people followed them. Then, when time lengthened and the Hawariyyun died, may Allah be pleased with them, people divided and corruption crept in among them; the people of falsehood prevailed and the people of truth became weak, until at the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ) they were nonexistent or in the state of non-existence, as the story of Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, indicates. Thus the end of the surah, as you see, returned to its beginning through what occurred of exoneration from what the exaltation of the disbelievers might suggest of deficiency, through the support of His allies and the subjugation of His enemies, and through the command, of which the opening informed that He loves it, concerning fighting in His way, as urging and as encouragement toward it, connecting with what He gave good tidings of to those who believed, even at the lowest aspects of faith, of honor, joining its end to its beginning, by what was removed of the causes that led him to compromise and the matters that caused him to go along with the disbelievers and to be accommodating. This necessitated the firm establishment of faith and the attainment of perfection, which requires the actual purification from every stain of deficiency. Allah is the Granter of success to what is right, and upon Him is reliance.
